import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from datetime import datetime

# Read the data
data = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Product Distribution (Bar chart)
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
product_counts = data['product'].value_counts()
colors_products = sns.color_palette('Set2', len(product_counts))
ax1.bar(product_counts.index, product_counts.values, color=colors_products)
ax1.set_title('Product Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Product')
ax1.set_ylabel('Count')
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Revenue by Product (Bar chart)
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
revenue_by_product = data.groupby('product')['total'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
colors_revenue = sns.color_palette('viridis', len(revenue_by_product))
ax2.bar(revenue_by_product.index, revenue_by_product.values, color=colors_revenue)
ax2.set_title('Revenue by Product', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Product')
ax2.set_ylabel('Total Revenue ($)')
ax2.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 3. Payment Method Distribution (Pie chart)
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
payment_counts = data['payment_method'].value_counts()
colors_payment = sns.color_palette('pastel', len(payment_counts))
ax3.pie(payment_counts.values, labels=payment_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', 
        colors=colors_payment, startangle=90)
ax3.set_title('Payment Methods', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 4. Customer Age Group Distribution (Horizontal bar)
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
age_counts = data['customer_age_group'].value_counts().sort_values()
colors_age = sns.color_palette('coolwarm', len(age_counts))
ax4.barh(age_counts.index, age_counts.values, color=colors_age)
ax4.set_title('Customer Age Groups', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Count')
ax4.set_ylabel('Age Group')

# 5. Size Distribution (Pie chart)
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
size_counts = data['size'].value_counts()
colors_size = sns.color_palette('Set3', len(size_counts))
ax5.pie(size_counts.values, labels=size_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%',
        colors=colors_size, startangle=90)
ax5.set_title('Size Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 6. Takeaway vs Dine-in (Pie chart)
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
takeaway_counts = data['is_takeaway'].value_counts()
takeaway_labels = ['Takeaway' if x == 1 else 'Dine-in' for x in takeaway_counts.index]
colors_takeaway = ['#ff9999', '#66b3ff']
ax6.pie(takeaway_counts.values, labels=takeaway_labels, autopct='%1.1f%%',
        colors=colors_takeaway, startangle=90)
ax6.set_title('Order Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 7. Price Distribution (Histogram)
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
ax7.hist(data['price'], bins=10, color='steelblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax7.set_title('Price Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax7.set_xlabel('Price ($)')
ax7.set_ylabel('Frequency')

# 8. Quantity Distribution (Histogram)
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
ax8.hist(data['quantity'], bins=range(1, int(data['quantity'].max())+2), 
         color='coral', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax8.set_title('Quantity Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax8.set_xlabel('Quantity')
ax8.set_ylabel('Frequency')

# 9. Total Revenue Distribution (Histogram)
ax9 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
ax9.hist(data['total'], bins=10, color='mediumseagreen', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax9.set_title('Total Revenue Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax9.set_xlabel('Total ($)')
ax9.set_ylabel('Frequency')

# Main title
fig.suptitle('Coffee Shop Sales Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
